I believe that in large part due to people relocating due to work, cost of living, or other reasons as well as modern forms of media and communication (the internet being the best example) it no longer makes sense to think of minorities as something to represent based on region. There are some conservatives living in San Francisco and liberals in rural Mississippi so I think it's important to make those people feel like their vote matters. So abolish the electoral college using a winner take all national popular vote (so say a Republican in California can still feel like their vote matters) while electing the senate through proportional representation to represent the minority groups. This means that instead of each state having a local popular vote to decide their senators the entire nation will elect 100 senators as a whole with 1% of the vote equaling 1 seat in the senate. So if the people of the USA vote 50% Republican, 40% Democrat, 8% Libertarian, 2% Green than the senate will have 50 Republicans, 40 Democrats, 8 Libertarians, and 2 Greens. And these parties can get together and form coalition governments (in countries that use this system it's not uncommon to have dozens of parties who each only get a few percent of the vote). This will mean that a conservative in a rural state will not be totally drowned out by liberal voters in San Francisco though a conservative in a liberal state or a liberal in a conservative state can vote against the overwhelming majority of said state and know it will count. It also means a party seen as corrupt is more likely to get tossed out of power at the drop of a hat when people vote for a different party whose views they find at least tolerable and whom they see as less corrupt. Also you can vote for the party whom represent your views more rather than having to be forced to compromise on a more "electable" moderate party and know your party will carry more weight in a coalition and in the government in general when they gain more votes.

This is also good because Republicans who like Donald Trump and Democrats who like Bernie Sanders tend not to align entirely with the mainstream figures of their party. Trump could've still won without the electoral college I think (I'm not saying this idea because I want Clinton to win. I can't say I like either of them personally) but we won't know for sure unless the system is changed. As someone said in the comments https://voat.co/v/politics/1515342/7358699 it would probably mean a 7 way race for the senate and presidency so things would look very, very different to the point it's hard to discuss.
